_comment: One-way ceiling on oversized source files, per package. The number is Σ max(0, lines − 500) — the total lines past the limit, NOT a file count, so splitting a large file always lowers it and never trips the gate. check-file-size-ratchet.ts fails when a package's number RISES. After splitting something, run `pnpm lint:file-size --update` to lock the win; --update never raises a floor. Raising a number requires editing this file in the same PR.
_apps_api_src_note: 44016 → 44022 (+6) for the role-scoped case visibility in ai-agent/tools: the guard plus the two constraints recorded on it (read the role never cache it; absent role is no role). Prettier reflows the wider where-clauses onto extra lines, so trimming comments to fit does not survive the pre-commit format pass — not worth playing that game against a formatter. Earlier: 43947 → 44016 (+69). Extending G4 to ai-agent surfaced four defects and 41 sites needing a written justification; the annotations, the two access-control fixes in ai-agent/tools, the owner predicates in task-queue, the small-cohort suppression in analyzeIntlCompetitiveness, and the anonymizeProfile regression test all land in files already past 500 lines. Rationale was moved to .claude/rules/backend.md wherever it was policy rather than local detail; what is left is the guards themselves. Splitting a service to fit a comment budget would be the ratchet driving the design, so this is raised deliberately — it is guards and comments, not new behaviour, and the next split should take it back down.
_apps_api_prisma_note: 11948 → 11953 (+5) for the Penn testing-policy row. The 2026-07-24 audit held Penn at UNKNOWN pending an August recheck; the recheck landed and the row plus its evidence note is what grew the seed. The alternative to raising this is splitting seed-testing-policy-2026-07-25.ts, which would put a five-line data row behind a file split — the ratchet driving the design rather than the other way round. The oversized file here is seed-all-features.ts (3458 lines); that is the one worth splitting, and doing so takes this number back down.
